body:
OBSERVED in cps/kobo.py and a real-handler regression: each request initialized its outgoing archive cursor to datetime.min, advanced it only for archive rows and tombstones inspected in that request, then unconditionally serialized it. With no ArchivedBook rows and five acknowledged deletion tombstones, one request advanced the cursor through all five deletions and the next empty pass reset it to datetime.min. Repeating the returned tokens reproduced an exact latest/epoch alternation. This is the server-side producer of the partial-token condition whose entitlement replay risk is mitigated by F-e0843b and #2131.

OBSERVED fix: the outgoing archive field now starts at the incoming value, so an empty pass cannot move it backward. The timestamp arm still compares against the original incoming value, while a missing acknowledged tombstone row for the physical device independently admits backdated deletions. Real-handler regressions prove that an unseen deletion below the timestamp high-watermark is delivered exactly once and that 101 missing-ledger tombstones drain as bounded pages of 100 then one. #2131 same-reader fingerprint suppression remains enabled and unchanged.

ASSUMED: the repeated live-instance alternation reported during investigation has this exact code cause. The handler sequence reproduces its token and tombstone pattern, but this change was not exercised against a physical reader in this implementation pass.

resolution.note: Preserve the incoming archive field as the outgoing floor; use the original timestamp or a missing physical-device acknowledgment to select tombstones.

title: Kobo archive cursor regresses on empty archive passes
